RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Foster
Member ID: W899181963
Reference Number: POC-4825AA1F8B-42990
Service: Lumbar disc decompression/discectomy, CPT 63030
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-10
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-06

Dear Appeals Review Team,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar decompression with discectomy), denied on 2026-08-10 on the stated basis that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting additional clinical documentation below and request that the plan reverse this determination.

**Policy applied**
I understand the plan's clinical policy for this procedure is Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures, Reference Number CP.MP.114 (Date of Last Revision: 04/25), which is listed on Ambetter of Oklahoma's Clinical & Payment Policies page. That policy states:

"It is the policy of health plans affiliated with Centene Corporation® that open discectomy and microdiscectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following: A. Age ≥ 18 years; B. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc; C. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following: 1. Radiculopathy with motor deficit and one of the following: a. Severe weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by: a score of ≤ 3 on the Medical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale, or the inability to ambulate; b. Mild to moderate weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by a score of 4 on the Medical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale and one of the following: i. Worsening weakness or motor deficit; ii. Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following: a) ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate; b) ≥ four weeks activity modification; c) One of the following: 1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; 2) Epidural steroid injection; 2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy including all the following: a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate; b. ≥ four weeks activity modification; c. One of the following: i. NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; ii. Epidural steroid injection."

I have not independently verified that this document — rather than a delegated vendor's guideline — is the exact criteria set used to review this specific request, since Ambetter of Oklahoma has stated it may delegate utilization management for musculoskeletal/spine surgery to a vendor. I am asking the plan to confirm in writing which specific criteria document(s) were used for this determination. In the meantime, the enclosed records demonstrate that my case satisfies the CP.MP.114 criteria quoted above, element by element:

**A. Age ≥ 18 years:** [Please confirm from enrollment/demographic records on file; date of birth not included in the clinical packet summarized here.]

**B. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc:** MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-07-05 documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion.

**C. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging:** The same MRI documents severe right lateral recess stenosis with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root — imaging-confirmed nerve root compression at a level that corresponds directly to my clinical symptoms.

**C.2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit:** I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf, consistent with pain in a nerve root distribution, and on examination I have a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged L4-L5/L5 level, together with positive provocative testing on the affected side. This satisfies the "radiculopathy with sensory deficit" pathway, which requires:

- "≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate" — I completed 14 weeks (2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20) of supervised physical therapy, 20 visits, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This is well in excess of the four-week minimum.
- "≥ four weeks activity modification" — [Please see attached physical therapy and surgeon's notes documenting activity modification during this same period; if a distinct activity-modification note is required, we ask the plan to specify what additional documentation format it needs.]
- "NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated" or "Epidural steroid injection" — I have been on NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, far exceeding the three-week minimum, and I also received a corticosteroid (epidural) injection on 2026-05-18 that provided only 2 weeks of partial relief. Either of these independently satisfies this element of the criteria.

If my treating surgeon's exam findings also support a motor-deficit pathway (C.1) — for example, a specific Medical Research Council muscle strength grade in the L5/S1 distribution — I am asking Dr. Okafor to submit that grading directly, as the summary of records available to me states only that I have "a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level" without a specific motor grade. [Specific MRC muscle strength score, if applicable, to be supplied by treating surgeon.] Regardless, the sensory-deficit pathway above (C.2) does not require a motor deficit or MRC grading and is fully supported by the enclosed records.

**Functional impact:** I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time because of this condition, which further documents the severity and functional limitation caused by the L4-L5 disc extrusion and nerve root compression.

**Other relevant history:** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker — none of which are stated exclusions under CP.MP.114.

**Symptom duration:** My symptoms have been present and progressive for 9 months, unrelieved by rest, which is consistent with the persistence of symptoms addressed by the conservative-care requirements above.

Given this record, I believe the documentation now submitted directly addresses each element of the CP.MP.114 medical-necessity criteria for open discectomy/microdiscectomy that corresponds to CPT 63030, and I request that the denial be reversed and the prior authorization approved.

Enclosed with this appeal:
1. Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20, 20 visits)
2. Medication/treatment records documenting 6 months of NSAID therapy
3. Record of epidural/corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-18 and outcome
4. MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-07-05
5. Surgeon Dr. Okafor's clinical exam notes, including provocative testing and neurologic findings
6. [Any additional records the surgeon can provide specifying motor strength grading, if available]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the specific policy or guideline document(s), including title, reference/guideline number, and effective date, that were used to review my original request, per my right to the evidence relied upon in this determination. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-06 (180 days from the date of the denial notice).

I can be reached at [phone number] and [email address] with any questions, and I am willing to have Dr. Okafor participate in a peer-to-peer review if that would help resolve this appeal promptly.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster
